messages:
sara_support: FYI customer AcmeBooks reporting weird behavior — console shows requests routing to us-east-1 but our request logs show eu-west-1. High latency for them. Can someone triage?

ingrid_sre: Noted. Do we have a sample request ID and timestamps?

sara_support: Yep, pasted from ticket: request_id=rw_0a1b2c3d4e, customer says observed at ~2026-03-17T14:12Z. They took a screenshot of Console -> Route: us-east-1.

mike_prod: Also seeing a spike in cross-region p95 for that customer. Linking quick metrics dump from jason. @jason_metrics can you share the trace?

jason_metrics: Attaching trace snippet (redacted):
```
measurements: {
  request_id: "rw_0a1b2c3d4e",
  observed_region_console: "us-east-1",
  served_from_log_header: "eu-west-1",
  latency_ms: 420,
  routing_policy: "region-pref:us-east-1, fallback:global"
}
```
Looks like the request was served from eu-west-1 despite console indicating us-east-1.

sara_support: The customer sees consistently high tail latency when console says us-east. They pay for dedicated cap in us-east. Billing & SLA implications. They want root cause.

ingrid_sre: First guess: control-plane display (console) not updated after quick fallback to nearest healthy capacity (we have fallback-to-region when capacity triggers). Need to confirm whether the serving layer appended x-redwood-region header. Can support ask customer to run a simple curl returning headers?

sara_support: Sent quick repro to customer: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` and asked them to paste response headers.

customer_headers (posted by support from ticket):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
x-request-id: rw_0a1b2c3d4e
x-routing-hint: us-east-1
```

mike_prod: Aha — x-routing-hint = us-east-1, but x-redwood-region = eu-west-1. That matches the mismatch. Looks like the request was routed to us-east preference but actually executed in eu-west. Need to check the smart-routing decision log and fallback triggers.

ingrid_sre: @deploy-bot any recent changes to routing config or failover TTL?

deploy-bot: [deploy] routing-service v2.14.1 deployed by @sam at 2026-03-17T13:59Z. Change: add dynamic-fallback-throttle flag.

ingrid_sre: That throttle flag could be causing immediate fallback to alternate region if capacity signals delay us-east. But why console still shows us-east? Console reads control-plane binding cached value (region pinned) and doesn't update on fast ephemeral fallback. We need to confirm cache invalidation path.

jason_metrics: I pulled the routing-service logs for rw_0a1b2c3d4e:
```
[2026-03-17T14:11:59Z] routing-decision request=rw_0a1b2c3d4e preferred=us-east-1 -> probe failed (pending 180ms)
[2026-03-17T14:12:00Z] fallback->eu-west-1 reason=probe_timeout
[2026-03-17T14:12:00Z] emit header x-routing-hint=us-east-1 x-redwood-region=eu-west-1
```
So routing-service made a fallback. Console likely uses last pinned region (us-east-1) from the deploy plan, not the live ephemeral fallback.

sara_support: Customer understandably upset that console shows us-east (they paid for reserved in us-east). How do we respond re: billing/SLA?

ingrid_sre: Short-term: clarify to customer that reserved capacity pinning is at the tenancy level (they are pinned to us-east for dedicated capacity), but ephemeral failover to eu-west for a small percentage of requests can happen when us-east capacity probes fail. We should offer a breakdown (percent of requests served from other regions) and remediation steps: raise their guaranteed capacity or enable strict-routing (no-fallback) for an SLA hit.

mike_prod: We should also flag product bug: Console should surface these ephemeral fallbacks in the route details / live traffic pane. File a ticket to product to show last 5 minutes actual serving regions.

jason_metrics: For this request window I can compute customer-level served-region distribution and share. Early estimate: ~3.2% of requests to eu-west during 14:10-14:20Z window.

ingrid_sre: Action items: (1) @jason_metrics produce per-customer served-region percent and attach to ticket, (2) @mike_prod open product issue for console live-region visibility, (3) engineering to review dynamic-fallback-throttle behavior (I will take).

sara_support: Logged to ticket #SUP-12847 and notified customer of investigation and options. Sending them the header evidence + suggested mitigations. They asked for ETA on fix for console visibility.

ingrid_sre: ETA: quick UX change (surface recent serve regions) is product + frontend work, estimate 2 sprints. Engineering fix to make control-plane reflect ephemeral fallbacks in a separate lightweight stream could be faster — I'll propose a small shim to emit fallback events to the console websocket.

mike_prod: Also recommend adding an admin metric for percent served outside pinned region that can trigger automatic alerts for customers and us.

sara_support: Thanks all — I'll update ticket with the plan and next steps. Customer requested a formal writeup; I'll paste your explanations and the trace + metrics when ready. :thumbsup:

ingrid_sre: One more note: please ask customer to include both the x-routing-hint and x-redwood-region headers next time, and if they can run `curl -s -D - https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` to capture headers. That will help in root cause.

sara_support: Will do. Closing loop for now.
